findings.title: Owner liveness rule ('no zombie') takes a live owner whose main thread exited as dead: two processes then write one mirror
findings.problem:
The diff fixes the liveness rule in two places. The header says owner_alive means 'the recorded pid's process exists and is no zombie'. S2.10 maps 'dead or zombie' to takeover. Plan D11c checks this with `/proc/<pid>/stat` not Z or X. That file shows the state of the thread-group leader only. When a CUDA application's main thread calls pthread_exit while its other threads (and the agent's delivery thread) keep running, the leader is Z and the process is fully alive.

Interleaving:
1. Owner A's main thread has exited. A's delivery thread keeps running apply_delivery.
2. Process B calls claim(). alive(A) is false (Z), so B CASes OWNER from A to B and takes the takeover path.
3. B's takeover_image reads the mirror while A's pass C is writing it.
4. Both processes now run apply_delivery on the same mirror. The 'one writer at a time' rule (hpp:31-33) is broken, and the guard's relaxed reads of 'its own stores' (cpp:453-457) no longer hold.

Concrete wrong results:
- K1 has 100 on A's device and the takeover seed plus B's adds, say 60, on B's device. B's pass A stores 60 over A's 100, so a CPU lookup sees the value drop (rule (b) broken).
- A key B inserts at a slot where A's device later puts another live key is never shown: the guard keeps A's live header.
- Each process's GPU adds go to its own device copy.

The liveness function itself is S5's to write, but the rule it must follow is set by this diff.
findings.evidence:
/tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-review/zombie/z.c: a forked child creates a sleeping worker thread, then calls pthread_exit in main. Output:
```
/proc/4015675/task/4015675 Z
/proc/4015675/task/4015676 S
kill(pid,0)=0 errno=0  /proc/pid/stat state='Z'
```
So kill(pid,0) succeeds while /proc/<pid>/stat reports Z and a thread of the process is running. With claim()'s alive callback following D11c, cpp:245-249 computes owner_alive=false, and devhash_choose_path (cpp:101-108) returns takeover for phase 2.
findings.suggested_change: Count the owner alive while any of its tasks is not Z/X. Ways to check: scan `/proc/<pid>/task/*/stat`, or read Threads in `/proc/<pid>/status`. Better, record the delivery thread's tid next to OWNER and probe it as ringbuf's is_thread_gone does. Add the process start time (stat field 22) to the owner record, so that an unrelated process that reuses the pid is not taken for a live owner (which today means not_owner forever). Change the header comment and test:999 to match, and add a test case: an owner child whose main thread called pthread_exit while another thread runs is alive.

findings.title: An ordinary exit of a multi-threaded writer process leaves INFLIGHT above 0 for good: no later seal ever succeeds
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:176-210 (increment in writer_enter, decrement after the table op), 275-307 (seal); PLAN-stage1.md:153-163 (D8)
findings.problem: D8 names a dead writer as the case that leaves INFLIGHT raised, implicitly a rare SIGKILL during an update. An ordinary process exit (exit() or _exit(), i.e. exit_group) kills sibling threads wherever they are, so every exit of a traced or tool process whose other threads are inside elem_update or elem_delete is such a death. This covers the unlocked parts of the window and the EPERM path, not only the moments a stripe or free-list lock is held. Nothing ever decrements a dead thread's count. After that, every seal and recover_sealing times out (PHASE 1 for up to 1 s, then PHASE 0 and SEAL_DEAD), and later attempts return seal_dead because INFLIGHT never reads 0 again. The map has no device copy for the rest of the segment's life: GPU lookups return NULL and inserts -1, and there is no recovery short of recreating the segment. Leaks on the EPERM path during a phase-1 window (a seal, or a dead sealer's PHASE 1) make recover_sealing time out the same way. Leaks in phase 2 are harmless today, because devhash_choose_path reads INFLIGHT only together with SEAL_DEAD. Exits that left a lock held are the existing, documented dead-holder hazard. The new part is the INFLIGHT-only leaks, where the table works but the map can never be copied.
findings.evidence:
Harness /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-review/exitleak/exitleak3.cpp, linked against build-cuda/runtime/libruntime.a. Each child gets a fresh 8 MB segment and map, 4 threads loop {elem_update BPF_ANY; spin gap}, and main exits after 5 ms. A deadline-bounded updater then checks whether a lock was left held. Results:
```
phase 0 _exit, gap 1000 ns: 23 of 40 exits left INFLIGHT above 0; locks left held in 6
phase 0 _exit, gap 10000 ns: 8 of 40 exits left INFLIGHT above 0; locks left held in 6
phase 0 exit, gap 1000 ns: 30 of 40 ...; locks left held in 11
phase 0 exit, gap 10000 ns: 10 of 40 ...; locks left held in 5
phase 2 (EPERM path) _exit, gap 1000 ns: 23 of 40 ...; locks left held in 0
```
A held lock implies a raised INFLIGHT, so 2-5 of 40 exits at a 10 us gap, and 17-19 of 40 at 1 us, leaked INFLIGHT with every lock free. After such leaks (exitleak.cpp, shared map): `seal after the exits: failed in 200 ms, SEAL_DEAD 1, phase 0`.
findings.suggested_change: Make in-flight writers recoverable. One way: register each writer in a slot keyed by (pid namespace, pid, tid), as ringbuf's reservation_owner table does, or keep one counter per process slot. On a poll timeout the sealer then discounts slots whose thread or process is gone (tgkill ESRCH, or Z/X in the task's stat) instead of declaring SEAL_DEAD. If the design stays as it is, write in the README that any exit of a process with threads writing the map in phase 0 (CPU probes) can disable the device copy for the segment's life, and add a test that exits a writer process normally.

findings.title: After a seal timeout, OWNER stays with the live sealer: D8's 'later attempt (any process)' cannot happen, and S2.4 bypasses claim()
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:254-264 (claim returns seal_dead after its CAS), 290-300 (seal timeout), 101-110 (live-owner check before SEAL_DEAD); nv_gpu_device_hash_map.hpp:153-157; runtime/unit-test/maps/test_gpu_device_hash.cpp:496-506; PLAN-stage1.md:159-163, 298, 372
findings.problem:
The plan is ambiguous on whether a seal timeout gives the claim back, and the code under review leaves OWNER held on both no-copy paths.

What the plan says:
- D8's timeout list (plan:159-160) does not release OWNER: PHASE 0, SEAL_DEAD, block freed, return 0.
- D11d (plan:298) releases only 'on a failed first copy or takeover (D15)'.
- D15's 'What counts' (plan:372) lists the copy, the synchronize and registration, not the seal.
- Yet D8 (plan:161) says 'A later attempt (any process) that sees SEAL_DEAD reads INFLIGHT once'.

What the code does:
- claim() can return seal_dead after its own CAS succeeded, with OWNER = self (cpp:262-264). The header (hpp:153-157) does not say the caller must call release_claim then.
- seal() does not release on a timeout.
- devhash_choose_path checks for a live same-namespace owner (cpp:101-108) before SEAL_DEAD (cpp:109-110). So while the sealer lives, every other process gets not_owner, even after the stalled writer has finished and INFLIGHT is 0.

The map then has no device copy in any process until the sealer process itself runs init again or dies.

S2.4's 'second attempt, from another process' (test:496-506) calls seal_and_build directly, so it passes where a real second agent, going through claim(), would get not_owner.
findings.evidence:
Harness /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-review/claimheld/claimheld.cpp, against libruntime.a:
- A writer child is SIGSTOPped in its update.
- Agent A runs claim() then seal_and_build(100 ms), and stays alive.
- The writer is SIGCONTed and finishes.
- Agent B runs claim() with a kill(pid,0) liveness callback.
Output:
```
A (pid 4018965): claim -> first_copy, seal_and_build -> 0, SEAL_DEAD 1, owner pid 4018965
writer finished (status 0); INFLIGHT 0
B (pid 4018973), A alive: claim -> not_owner
B2 (pid 4018974), A dead: claim -> first_copy
```
findings.suggested_change: Settle it in the plan (D8, D11d, D15): every path that ends without a copy gives the claim back, including a seal timeout and claim() returning seal_dead after its CAS. Then do it in code: release_claim on those paths, either inside seal_and_build/recover_sealing or as a documented duty of the S5 caller, and note it in the claim() comment. Run S2.4's second attempt through claim() in another process while the first sealer process is still alive, and expect it to seal once INFLIGHT is 0.

findings.title: S2.7's 'reader in another process' runs only after all deliveries and readers have finished: it cannot fail for concurrent cross-process reads
findings.file_line: runtime/unit-test/maps/test_gpu_device_hash.cpp:847-863; PLAN-stage1.md S2.7 ('Run once more with the readers in a forked process on the same segment')
findings.problem: The plan asks for the random run to be repeated with its readers in a forked process, so that rules (a)-(d) are checked while deliveries run. The test does something else. It sets stop = true, joins r1 and r2, and only then forks a child that checks, for each key, that a lookup returns a value of at least the first staged value. Nothing is delivered while the child runs. So the child checks neither (a) found-then-missing, nor (c) the DELIVERIES marker, nor (d) get_next_key followed by lookup, and no ordering between the writer and a reader in another process is ever exercised. The comment 'the same rules from a reader in another process' claims more than the code checks.
findings.suggested_change: Fork the reader processes before the delivery loop. Each runs the same reader loop (DELIVERIES acquire, the per-delivery live sets kept in the shared segment, rules a-d, a step bound) until a stop word in shm is set, then exits with the failure count. Bound the run with in_child's deadline. Optionally map the segment at a different address in an exec'd child, so that offset_ptr use in mhdr() and mval() is covered too.

findings.title: check_devhash_orders.sh checks only sealer_enter's first INFLIGHT load; seal()'s polls can be made relaxed and the script still says OK
findings.problem: When writers are in flight at the PHASE store, the seal ends on one of the loop's polls (cpp:288, 292), or on the SEAL_DEAD path's load (cpp:280), not on sealer_enter's first load. A poll that reads 0 must at least acquire: it has to synchronize with the writers' release decrements. Otherwise build_image's scan is not ordered after their table writes, and on the Orin (loads to different addresses may be reordered) it can read an element word from before a writer's insert and leave that key out of the image. The script reads only bpftime_devhash_sealer_enter, so S2.12 does not cover these loads, and S2.3 cannot be expected to catch such a mutation on hardware.
findings.evidence: A copy with both polls changed to __ATOMIC_RELAXED (/tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-review/orders/relaxed_polls.cpp; diff: lines 288 and 292 SEQ_CST -> RELAXED) passed the script: `bash check_devhash_orders.sh build-cuda relaxed_polls.cpp` printed `sealer: ... stlr x2, [x0]; ldar x0, [x1]; ret` and `OK`.
findings.suggested_change: Move the poll load into its own extern "C" noinline function (for example bpftime_devhash_sealer_poll) and use it at cpp:280, 288 and 292. Have the script require LDAR or LDAPR there, not LDR, and add a relaxed-poll mutation to S2.12.

findings.title: The 'writer_after_inflight_inc' hook fires after the PHASE load, so no test stops a writer between its increment and its PHASE load
findings.file_line: runtime/src/bpf_map/gpu/nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:180-182, 198-200; PLAN-stage1.md S2 test hooks ('park a writer after its PHASE load; park a writer after its INFLIGHT increment')
findings.problem: The plan lists two distinct parking points. In the code both hooks are called back to back, after bpftime_devhash_writer_enter has done both the increment and the PHASE load: `const uint64_t ph = bpftime_devhash_writer_enter(&inflight, &phase); call_hook(writer_after_inflight_inc, ph); call_hook(writer_after_phase_load, ph);`. Every test that parks or kills 'after the increment' (S2.4 dead and stopped writers, S2.11's second case) has in fact also read PHASE 0. S2.4's stopped-writer comment says so ('it read phase 0 before it stopped'). D8's argument is about the state in between: the increment is visible and PHASE is not yet read, so the sealer must wait and the writer must then get EPERM. No test covers that state. Only the disassembly script guards the order there.
findings.evidence: cpp:180-182 and 198-200 as quoted; test:550-560 (the stopped writer 'read phase 0 before it stopped: the update goes through').
findings.suggested_change: Call the increment hook inside bpftime_devhash_writer_enter, between the fetch_add and the PHASE load (a test-only pointer load, null in production), and adjust the script to skip that load. Add a case: a writer stopped there while a sealer stores PHASE 1. The seal must wait; on release the writer must get EPERM and the seal must complete with the key absent.

findings.title: A full directory makes every delivery's repair superlinear and every CPU lookup miss walk all slots (in the traced process)
findings.problem:
This is outside the concurrency lens. Refused and claiming slots are permanent (D4), so 2 x max_entries distinct keys fill the directory. On a full directory:
- Repair walks from home to slot for every keyed slot on every delivery, even when nothing changed. Total work is the directory's total displacement, which for linear probing at load 1 grows about as S^1.5.
- Each delivery also allocates two vectors of S u64 (cpp:443).
- mirror_find stops only at an empty slot or live K, so a CPU lookup of an absent key walks all S slots with acquire loads.
Both run in the traced process: the deliveries in the agent's thread under run_mutex, and the lookups in CPU probes.
findings.evidence:
Harness /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-review/full/full.cpp: random distinct keys are inserted into a model of the device directory until it is full (max_entries live, the rest refused), then delivered.
- Repair steps, which are deterministic: 37,644,635 at max_entries 65,536 (131,072 slots) and 265,396,344 at 262,144 (524,288 slots).
- Measured with another job holding a core at 100%: apply_delivery 66 ms and about 450 ms, the same for a second, unchanged delivery. One CPU lookup miss: 1.02 ms and 4.15 ms.
- Extrapolation, not measured: at 2^22 entries, tens of seconds per delivery and tens of ms per miss.
findings.suggested_change: Repair in one circular O(S) pass: walk the slots once from a known empty slot, tracking the current run's start, and mark staged-empty slots inside a run that a later keyed slot's home precedes. Or repair only around slots that changed since the last delivery, and reuse the staging buffers. Bound mirror_find by the largest probe distance the delivery has seen (kept in the map object) instead of S.

D11c prescribes '`/proc/<pid>/stat` is not Z or X', and that file shows the thread-group leader's state only. A process whose main thread called pthread_exit therefore reads Z while its other threads, the agent's delivery thread among them, keep running. Given owner_alive=false, the code takes over: claim() at cpp:245-249 and choose_path at cpp:101-108 then reach `default: return devhash_path::takeover` for phase 2. Nothing in the plan covers this case. ringbuf's is_thread_gone, which D11c cites, probes a specific /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stat. Applied to the leader only, it misjudges the whole process.

findings.title: No S2 test checks that a later delivery updates a key's value in the mirror; a mutant that keeps only the first value passes them all
findings.problem: Plan rule S2.7(b) says a found value is never below the value staged with that header. The test checks only the value staged the first time a key is live: `first.emplace(key_of(hh), dev.sum[s])` never overwrites, and both the readers and the forked child compare against `first`. Every exact-value check also follows a key's first delivery: section 1 (`*v == 7`), section 3 (`== 99`), key 0 (`== 12`), and S2.9 (one delivery). Pass A refreshing the sums of already-live slots is what the CPU reads in phase 2, and no test covers it.
findings.evidence: Harness in /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-review/plan-and-tests. The test file is unchanged apart from dropping S2.1 and adding counters: 4,723 assertions = 4,739 minus S2.1's 16. It links the built fix_hash_map.cpp.o and friends with a copy of nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp. Mutant dh_passA.cpp, pass A condition: `state_of(hdr[s]) == ST_LIVE && __atomic_load_n(mhdr() + s, __ATOMIC_RELAXED) != hdr[s] && __atomic_load_n(mval() + s, __ATOMIC_RELAXED) != val[s]`. Values are then written only when a slot's header changes, so sums freeze at the first delivery. `./t_passA "[gpu-devhash-cpu]"` -> "All tests passed (4723 assertions in 11 test cases)".
findings.suggested_change: Record each key's value per staging (live_at as key -> value). A reader that acquired DELIVERIES >= N checks that the value it finds is at least staging N's value. Add a deterministic case: deliver K=5, then K=9, and require *get(K) == 9. Mutation: values written only when the header changes.

findings.title: The owner liveness rule (D11c), the namespace id (D11b) and their test stubs are missing; S2.10's EPERM and zombie rows are plain bools, and the plan's EPERM mutation is silently dropped
findings.problem: Plan S2 lists the hooks "a liveness stub; a namespace stub". S2.10 asks for "a live owner, a dead owner, an EPERM-alive owner, a zombie owner" with the mutation "EPERM taken as dead". The code has no liveness function (kill(pid,0) taking EPERM as alive, /proc/<pid>/stat Z/X as dead) and no namespace-id function (inode of /proc/self/ns/pid, or a random id). claim() takes `alive` as a caller-supplied std::function, and choose_path takes a bool. The test's `path(2, other, true) // alive (EPERM too)` and `path(2, other, false) // dead or zombie` pass bools, so they cannot fail for EPERM-as-dead or zombie-as-alive. S2-result.md reports "19 mutations" and lists only "cached copy treated as a takeover" for S2.10. The plan's "EPERM taken as dead" is neither run nor mentioned: of the plan's 20 S2 mutations, 18 were run, plus one extra (key compared before state). The plan may have meant the stubs for S5's use, but no deferral is recorded.
findings.evidence: `git diff 7d02d677..192f08d7 -- runtime/src attach/nv_attach_impl/trampoline | grep -E '^\+.*(kill\(|/proc|ns/pid|_for_test|is_thread_gone|alive)'` finds only set_devhash_hook_for_test, force_phase_for_test, table_for_test and the `owner_alive`/`alive` parameters: no kill(), no /proc, no ns/pid. mutations.txt has no EPERM entry.
findings.suggested_change: Implement the D11c liveness check (kill + /proc stat, as is_thread_gone does) and the D11b namespace id in S2, each with a `*_for_test` stub setter. Test S2.10 through the real function, stubbing kill's result (EPERM) and the stat state (Z). Run the EPERM-as-dead mutation, or record in S2-result.md that it moves to S5.

findings.title: apply_delivery re-walks every keyed slot's whole probe path on every delivery: seconds per delivery on a full directory at large max_entries
findings.problem: The repair loop walks home(K)..j for every keyed staged slot on every delivery, even when nothing changed since the last one. Its cost is the directory's total linear-probing displacement, which grows quickly as the directory nears full. DESIGN.md:31 makes a full directory an expected state: "the table fills once the distinct keys tried reach the slot count ... Any undersized map hits this". Each delivery also allocates two vectors of 8*S bytes (128 MB at max_entries 2^22). In S5 this runs under run_mutex, and with BPFTIME_GPU_DELIVERY_AT_SYNC=1 inside the application's synchronize call (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:665-680). The plan's S8 delivery-cost rule measures only max_entries 512 and 1024 with all rows live, so it would not see this. Major, not blocker: S5 is not built yet.
findings.evidence: bench.cpp in /tmp/claude-2002/devhash-s2-review/plan-and-tests calls the committed apply_delivery (dh_orig.o) on a device-model staging, with M live and the rest refused. Steady-state deliveries (the same staging again) take the same time. max_entries 2^16, fill 1.0: 42 ms. 2^18: fill 0.75 23 ms, 0.90 25 ms, 0.99 60 ms, 1.0 383 ms. 2^20: 0.5 83 ms, 0.75 86 ms, 0.90 94 ms, 0.99 244 ms, 1.0 3,660 ms (total displacement 2.2e9). At 2^22, 4.7e10 displacement per delivery is extrapolated (about 10x per 4x of S), roughly 30+ s, not measured.
findings.suggested_change: Walk only the keyed staged slots whose mirror header does not already hold that key (new or changed slots). After the guard, every slot already in the mirror keeps a non-empty path. Keep the hdr/val buffers between deliveries. Add an S8 measurement of a full directory at large max_entries.

findings.title: S2.7's "run once more with the readers in a forked process" is not done: the child only checks first values after all deliveries
findings.problem: The plan wants the reader run repeated with readers in a forked process on the same segment, checking rules (a)-(d) while deliveries happen. The test forks one child after the writer and the thread readers have stopped (`stop = true; r1.join(); r2.join();` comes first). The child only checks `*v >= first value` for each key once. No reader in another process runs during a delivery, and rules (c) (marker) and (d) (get_next_key, then lookup) are never checked from another process.
findings.evidence: Test 852-863: `in_child([&]() { for (auto &[k, v0] : first) { auto *v = get(map, k); if (!v || *v < v0) return 3; } return 0; }, ...)` runs after the 400 rounds have finished.
findings.suggested_change: Fork the reader processes before the delivery loop, with the same loop as the thread readers, and have them report failures through the exit status or a shm counter. Stop them with a shm flag, under a deadline.

findings.title: S2.7's concurrent random run barely covers repair: 15 stale slots, all in the first 39 of 400 rounds, and no keyed-slot defensive staging
findings.problem: Plan S2.7 has the listed stagings (live K behind a staged-empty slot, claiming-caused repairs, keyed slots shown empty again) applied while readers run. In the random run, stale slots are picked only among newly filled slots whose mirror slot is empty (line 827). The 64-slot directory is full by round 38. After that, every delivery only adds to sums, which the readers check against first values only (finding 2). Keyed-slot defensive stagings never occur in it. The no-repair and no-guard mutations are caught only by the deterministic sections, which have no concurrent readers. The seed is fixed, so these numbers are the same on every run.
findings.evidence: Instrumented copy t2.cpp (counters only), `./t2_orig "The delivered mirror stays walkable"`: "keys with a stale slot on their path 1, of them wrapping across S-1 1; stale slots 15; rounds with a newly filled slot 39, last 38".
findings.suggested_change: Keep generating new slots through the run: a larger key range against a larger directory, or start over when the directory is full. Also stage keyed slots empty again, and claiming keys that turn live while their repaired slot stays staged empty, while the readers run.

findings.title: CPU tests that can hang run in the test process, not in a child with a deadline (D16)
findings.file_line: runtime/unit-test/maps/test_gpu_device_hash.cpp:900-906 (S2.8 full directory); 397, 1037 (REQUIRE(wait_parked()) with a joinable thread); 509-513 and 1095-1098 (seal timeouts in-process)
findings.problem: D16: "So does a CPU test that can hang". S2.8's full-directory lookup runs in-process: a walk without its S bound hangs the whole test binary instead of failing. S2.4's and S2.11's timeout seals run in-process too, so a broken deadline hangs. When `REQUIRE(wait_parked())` fails, it throws while `std::thread writer` is still joinable, so std::terminate aborts the binary. S2.5 uses fork(), not an exec'd child.
findings.evidence: Mutant dh_nobound.cpp (mirror_find with `for (;;)`): `timeout -s KILL 15 ./t_nobound "get_next_key in phase 2: live keys in slot order"` gives rc=137, killed with no result. The full tag run was killed at 60 s after S2.7.
findings.suggested_change: Run S2.8's full-directory part and the seal-timeout parts through in_child with a deadline, or through the exec'd-child pattern D16 names. Detach or join the parked threads before a failing REQUIRE can unwind.

findings.title: The writer's EPERM side of the seal has no deterministic test: the after-increment hook fires after the PHASE load, and the free-running writers often never overlap the seal
findings.problem: The plan lists two hooks, "park a writer after its INFLIGHT increment" and "after its PHASE load". Both call_hook calls come after bpftime_devhash_writer_enter, which has already loaded PHASE, so they are the same point. No test can park a writer between its increment and its PHASE load, so this case is never forced: the sealer stores PHASE 1 and sees INFLIGHT > 0, then the writer reads 1, backs out with EPERM, and the seal completes. Only S2.3's 8 free-running writers can reach it, and in the full tag they often finish before the seal.
findings.evidence: cpp:180-182: `const uint64_t ph = bpftime_devhash_writer_enter(&inflight, &phase); call_hook(writer_after_inflight_inc, ph); call_hook(writer_after_phase_load, ph);`. Instrumented harness, full [gpu-devhash-cpu] runs: "inserted 3200, EPERM 0" twice (t_orig, t_nobound), 152 EPERM once. Run alone, S2.3 got EPERM in 10 of 10 runs.
findings.suggested_change: Split bpftime_devhash_writer_enter so the after-increment hook sits between the increment and the PHASE load; check_devhash_orders.sh must still see LDADDAL then LDAR. Add a case: park after the increment, seal (it waits), release, and expect EPERM with the seal completing. Also check that the free-running writers saw at least one EPERM, or retry.

findings.title: S2.12's script checks the three helper functions, not the update, delete, lookup and get_next_key paths the plan names
findings.problem: The plan wants the writer's PHASE load checked "on the update and delete paths" and the reader load "on the lookup and get_next_key paths". The script disassembles only bpftime_devhash_writer_enter, sealer_enter and reader_phase. A path that stopped calling the helper, for example an inline relaxed or acquire PHASE load in elem_delete or map_get_next_key, would still pass. Today all four paths call the helpers (cpp:166, 180, 198, 216), and the script fails its three mutations.
findings.evidence: Reproduced on copies: the committed code prints `writer: ldaddal; ldar`, `sealer: stlr; ldar`, `reader: ldapr`, OK (exit 0). acq_poll fails with "sealer ... ldapr", acq_writer with "writer ... ldapr", rlx_reader with "reader ... ldr" (exit 1 each, from the FAILED line, not a compile error).
findings.suggested_change: Also check, in the object code, that nv_gpu_device_hash_map_impl::elem_update, elem_delete, elem_lookup and map_get_next_key each call their helper, with no other load of the phase word before that call.

findings.title: S2.9 leaves out the plan's insert-until-full check after seeding
findings.problem: Plan S2.9: "Then a host model inserts new keys until the directory is full. Every insert after that is an immediate E2BIG, never a full-directory wait." The test checks the seeded count for E=0 and E=1 (and E > max_entries in the first section), but never runs inserts on the seeded image. The property the count rule exists for, that the directory cannot fill while count < max_entries, is not checked directly.
findings.evidence: The section "the count when few slots are empty" ends with `CHECK(img.count == (empty == 0 ? M : M - 1));`. No model insert follows the takeover_image() call.
findings.suggested_change: Load img into device_model (hdr, count) and insert new keys until claim() fails. Assert that count >= max_entries at every insert after the last empty slot is taken, so each later insert is refused by the count and never waits on a full directory.

findings.title: Phase-2 get_next_key writes through a null next_key (SIGSEGV), where phase 0 returns EINVAL
findings.problem: In phase 2, map_get_next_key stores `*(uint32_t *)next_key = key_of(h)` without a check. Before the copy, the same call goes to fix_size_hash_map_impl::map_get_next_key, which returns -1 with EINVAL for next_key == nullptr (fix_hash_map.cpp:87-90). Nothing above checks it: bpftime_shm::bpf_map_get_next_key (bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:426-434) and the syscall server's BPF_MAP_GET_NEXT_KEY pass attr->next_key straight through. A tool calling bpf(BPF_MAP_GET_NEXT_KEY) with next_key 0 gets EINVAL before the first GPU copy and a SIGSEGV of its own process (the syscall server's host) after it. The null-key lookup has the same crash in both phases (bpftime_hash_map reads the key), so only next_key is new.

findings.suggested_change: Check next_key == nullptr (EINVAL) at the top of nv_gpu_device_hash_map_impl::map_get_next_key, before the phase switch, so both phases answer the same way. Extend S2.8 with the null case.

findings.title: Agent-side entry points can throw bad_alloc into the traced process; apply_delivery allocates 2 x slots words on every delivery
findings.problem: apply_delivery allocates `std::vector<uint64_t> hdr(slots), val(slots)` on every delivery: 2 x 8 x 2^23 = 128 MiB at max_entries 2^22, zero-filled and freed again each time. build_image and takeover_image assign vectors of slots words, and claim() takes a std::function. None is noexcept. Deliveries will run on the agent's delivery thread in the traced process (S5), and an uncaught std::bad_alloc there ends the host through std::terminate (CLAUDE.md invariant 1). No caller exists yet, and the plan says nothing about who catches, so this is a missing contract that S5/S6 must close, not a crash reachable today.
findings.evidence: nv_gpu_device_hash_map.cpp:443 `std::vector<uint64_t> hdr(slots), val(slots);`. Lines 315-316 and 378-379: `out.headers.assign(slots, 0); out.values.assign(slots, 0);`. `grep -rn "apply_delivery\|build_image\|takeover_image\|seal_and_build\|recover_sealing\|\.claim(" runtime attach` outside the map files and unit tests finds no callers. `grep -n "catch\|noexcept\|bad_alloc\|exception" PLAN-stage1.md` finds nothing.
findings.suggested_change: Write the contract into the header: either the S5/S6 callers catch std::exception and fail open (no delivery, or no copy plus rollback per D15), or these functions catch internally and return false. In apply_delivery, run the guard and repair on a per-map scratch allocated once at registration, or in place on the agent's own staging buffer, instead of 128 MiB of fresh heap per delivery.

Under Linux's default overcommit, a 64 MiB allocation rarely throws bad_alloc; memory pressure ends in the OOM killer instead. The practical cost is mostly 128 MiB of heap churn per delivery.
